_comment: The renewables county brief (plain-English county summaries): 3 to 5 bullets for the top of a county page and one or two sentences that open each page section. Hand-edited; no process writes it. scripts/county_briefs.py builds each county's fact sheet from the published tables in the shared format of scripts/brief_core.py (pinned by config/brief_format.lock); the brief-drafter agent writes the brief from that sheet alone, the brief-reviewer agent checks it blind, and brief_core.check refuses any brief that fails.

sections: one entry per portal section a brief can open, keyed by the portal's own section id (hawthorn-portal web/public/js/sections.js). 'facts' names the published table the section's facts come from. A portal that does not show a section hides its line and any bullet that rests on it.
refused: terms clients never see (data-centers scripts/refused_columns.py keeps the matching columns internal). A brief that uses one fails.

style: the house wording the drafter follows, from config/county_report.json and the case-study Key Takeaways. township: the sentence a brief uses for a state's township rule (config/county_zoning_authority.json, township_land_use).
style: Plain third person. Name Hawthorn only as Hawthorn, never as we or our.
Say what public bodies did, with the date and the body: adopted, extended, repealed, approved, denied, withdrew, filed.
Use the record's own words for the instrument: moratorium, ban, setback, height limit, noise limit, zoning amendment, siting ordinance.

Say 'on record' for what the published tables hold, and 'in force' only when currency is in_force. When currency is lapsed_unconfirmed, say the record's end date has passed and no later extension is on record; when it is pending, say the rule is proposed and not adopted, unless the record says the body adopted it and it has not taken effect: then say it was adopted and is not in force.
A record whose verification is not 'verified' is described as not yet checked against the instrument itself.
Outcomes of contested projects use the ladder's display words only: blocked, restricted, advanced, pending.
Dates as Month D, YYYY. Sizes as 45 MW, distances as 2,000 feet.
Never explain why something happened or say what will happen next. Upcoming dates are stated as dates (the moratorium runs to September 18, 2027).
Open the headline with the strongest rule in force, then the state's siting law, then projects and cases, then dates to watch.

township.no_zoning_power: Townships in {state} do not zone, so rules for unincorporated land come from the county.
township.where_county_unzoned: Townships in {state} may zone only where the county has no zoning.
township.own_rules_else_county: In {state}, a township with its own zoning decides siting there; other townships follow the county.
township.township_primary: In {state}, townships and towns are the zoning bodies, and the county has no general zoning role.

worklist._comment: Counties drafted first, then any county whose fact sheet changed, at most per_run counties each run. first lists county codes only, never who asked for them.
